tests: A claim that restates its passage must pass. If this fails, the judge is too strict and the system will have nothing to say.
claim: Healthy older people should get at least 1.0 to 1.2 g of protein per kilogram of body weight per day.

passage.quote: for healthy older people, the diet should provide at least 1.0–1.2 g protein/kg body weight/day

tests: A real paraphrase that stays inside what the passage says. Must pass, or the system can only ever quote verbatim. Needed alongside exact-restatement so a judge that rejects everything cannot pass this harness.
claim: ESPEN advises a minimum daily protein intake of 1.0 to 1.2 grams per kilogram of body weight for older people who are healthy.

passage.quote: for healthy older people, the diet should provide at least 1.0–1.2 g protein/kg body weight/day

tests: NEAR-MISS, and a real one: this is the exact error found in this project's own fixtures on 2026-10-04. The source's population is older people who are MALNOURISHED OR AT RISK OF MALNUTRITION BECAUSE OF illness. The claim silently widens that to anyone with an illness. A judge that passes this would have passed the mistake that produced this case.
claim: Older people with an acute or chronic illness should consume 1.2 to 1.5 g of protein per kilogram of body weight per day.

passage.quote: for older people who are malnourished or at risk of malnutrition because they have acute or chronic illness, the diet should provide 1.2–1.5 g protein/kg body weight/day

tests: NEAR-MISS. A finding stated for healthy older people, restated as universal. The passage is about the topic and does not establish the claim.
claim: Everyone over 65 needs 1.2 g of protein per kilogram per day.

passage.quote: for healthy older people, the diet should provide at least 1.0–1.2 g protein/kg body weight/day

tests: NEAR-MISS. The passage says requirements MAY be higher; the claim says they ARE. One word of drift, and the claim now says something no source says.
claim: Protein requirements are higher in older adults than the current recommended allowance.

passage.source_name: Administration for Community Living, Nutrition Needs for Older Adults
passage.quote: The Recommended Dietary Allowance for older adults is the same as younger adults, though emerging research suggests older adults may indeed require more protein.

tests: A number that appears nowhere in the passage. The claim is topically adjacent and numerically fabricated.
claim: Muscle mass declines by 8% per decade after the age of 30.

passage.quote: for healthy older people, the diet should provide at least 1.0–1.2 g protein/kg body weight/day

tests: The passage and claim share a subject and nothing else. Catches a judge that is really just scoring similarity.
claim: Older people should avoid carbohydrates in the evening.

passage.quote: for healthy older people, the diet should provide at least 1.0–1.2 g protein/kg body weight/day

tests: NEAR-MISS. An association in the passage, asserted as cause in the claim. This is the most common drift and the one a similarity check cannot catch.
claim: Higher protein intake from animal, red meat and processed animal sources causes health-related quality of life to deteriorate over 12 years.

passage.source_name: Matison et al., BMC Geriatrics 2022 (AusDiab 12-year prospective study)
passage.quote: There was no relationship between total dietary protein intake and HRQoL, but higher protein intakes from animal, red meat and processed animal sources were associated with a deterioration in HRQoL scores over 12 years.
